body:
Audited every list-aware server surface for authorization. Result: no exploitable
bypass — pull (delta) is scoped to member lists, push authorizes edits against the
item's STORED list_id (immutable, not a syncable field), and /lists, /members,
mint/revoke/leave, and redeem all gate correctly. Added a consolidated adversarial
HTTP test (test_non_member_cannot_access_a_list_in_any_way) proving read/enumerate/
edit/hijack/invite/forge are all denied.

Two non-blocking observations (optional hardening, not exploitable):
1. Resource-existence oracle: /sync item push returns 422 (unknown/ missing list)
   vs 403 (exists-but-not-member), distinguishable — inconsistent with the uniform
   403 used by /members. Not practical to exploit (122-bit UUID ids) and leaks only
   existence, never contents.
2. Email-bound invites rely on unverified email ownership: with a leaked invite
   link, an attacker could register/relabel to the invited email (if unregistered)
   and redeem. Inherent to the documented email-bound design; token is the primary
   secret; single-use + 7-day expiry + revocable + HMAC-signed mitigate.
title: Security review: a logged-in non-member cannot access a list in any way (server authz)
